title: Kernel registry schema + versioning for selector v2 (generate/review/promote flow)
creator: Grace Kim
description:
Background
Kernel auto-selection v2 moves kernel choice from heuristic-only logic to a table-driven selector. This ticket defines the kernel registry artifact (schema + versioning) and the process by which entries are generated, reviewed, and promoted. The key goals are: (1) deterministic behavior, (2) safe rollout/rollback, (3) ability to update table entries without code changes, and (4) strong validation to prevent bad entries from causing perf regressions or correctness issues.

Scope
- Define a versioned schema ("registry schema") and a separately versioned content revision ("registry revision").
- Implement validation rules to reject unsafe/invalid entries at load time.
- Define ownership + review flow (CODEOWNERS + required reviewers) for registry updates.
- Define promotion flow (experimental -> stable) aligned with perf-canary + benchmark-lab results.

Non-goals
- Kernel development or kernel ID definition (assumed to exist in runtime).
- End-user facing configuration surface (wired in ENG-3931); this ticket only defines the registry structure and lifecycle.

Proposed artifact + location
- Repo: redwood/runtime
- Path: runtime/config/kernel_registry/
  - kernel_registry.schema.v1.json (schema definition, used by validators + tooling)
  - kernel_registry.v1.<revision>.json (registry content, revisioned)
  - kernel_registry.v1.latest.json (symlink/alias file used by default builds; updated when a revision is promoted)

Definitions
- Schema version: integer, only changes when the structure changes (e.g., new fields). Example: "schema_version": 1.
- Registry revision: monotonically increasing integer or YYYYMMDD.N format representing content updates under the same schema. Example: "registry_revision": "20260206.1".

Schema v1 (high level)
Top-level fields:
- schema_version (int): 1
- registry_revision (string): e.g., 20260206.1
- generated_at (string, ISO-8601)
- generated_by (string): tool + git sha
- notes (string): freeform; short explanation of what changed
- entries (array)

Entry fields:
- model_family (string): canonical family id (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen, unknown)
- model_flags (string): normalized flags impacting kernel choice (e.g., gqa=true; sliding_window=false). For v1, stored as a stable, sorted key-value string.
- seq_bucket (string): canonical bucket id (e.g., prefill_short, prefill_long, decode_short, decode_long)
- gpu_class (string): normalized GPU class (e.g., L4, A10, A100, H100). Must match GPU normalization output from ENG-3925.
- kernel_id (string): runtime kernel identifier (e.g., "flashattn2_sm80_prefill", "xformers_decode_sm89").
- constraints (string): stable string describing hard constraints (e.g., "requires_sm>=80; max_kv=131072"). For v1, stored as an opaque string but validated by runtime-known tokens.
- priority (string): numeric string 0..N used for deterministic tie-breaking when multiple entries match.
- status (string): one of experimental|stable|deprecated
- rationale (string): short note (benchmark link or reason)

Matching + determinism
- The selector resolves to the best matching entry using a strict precedence order:
  1) model_family exact match (else fall back to model_family=unknown)
  2) model_flags exact match (else fall back to model_flags="")
  3) seq_bucket exact match (no wildcard in v1)
  4) gpu_class exact match (no wildcard in v1)
  5) if multiple remain, choose highest priority; ties broken lexicographically by kernel_id to ensure determinism
- No implicit wildcards in v1. This is intentional to reduce accidental matches across regimes.

Validation rules (must fail closed)
Load-time validation:
- schema_version must be supported (only 1 for runtime-1.19)
- registry_revision must match expected format
- entries must be non-empty
- for each entry:
  - model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_class, kernel_id required
  - seq_bucket must be in the allowlist
  - gpu_class must be in the allowlist
  - kernel_id must be known to the runtime build (or in a "safe kernel set" allowlist)
  - constraints tokens must be parseable; unknown tokens rejected
- uniqueness:
  - must not have duplicate (model_family, model_flags, seq_bucket, gpu_class) rows

Safety defaults
- If registry fails to load/validate: selector v2 must disable itself and defer to selector v1 (or safe kernel set) depending on feature flag config (owned by ENG-3931).
- If matching yields no entry: return a "safe kernel set" default (e.g., conservative baseline kernel) and emit a selector telemetry event with reason=no_match.

Generation flow (how entries are produced)
- Source of truth for proposals:
  - benchmark-lab outputs a candidate matrix (model_family x seq_bucket x gpu_class -> kernel_id + metrics)
  - runtime team can optionally seed initial entries manually for bootstrap
- Tooling:
  - small generator script (owned by kernel team) reads benchmark-lab artifact(s) and produces kernel_registry.v1.<revision>.json
  - generator must include "generated_by" and links in "notes"

Review flow
- PR required for any registry revision changes (content or schema).
- CODEOWNERS:
  - Runtime Kernels: Hiro Tanaka
  - Kernel selection leads: Grace Kim, Yuki Sato
  - Perf sign-off: Marcus Reed or Rina Kobayashi for changes labeled stable
- Required checks:
  - registry_lint (schema + validation + uniqueness)
  - unit test that loads registry in runtime and exercises known contexts
  - perf-canary dry run link required for promotion to stable

Promotion flow (experimental -> stable)
- New entries start as status=experimental.
- Promotion criteria to stable:
  - benchmark report shows no p95 regressions beyond budget for the targeted GPU/model/seq bucket
  - conformance tests pass for impacted kernels (ENG-3928)
  - at least one hosted canary region shows neutral or positive deltas for 24h
- Promotion mechanism:
  - change status field to stable, and update kernel_registry.v1.latest.json to point at the promoted revision
  - keep at least N-2 prior stable revisions in repo for rollback

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Schema v1 defined and checked into repo
- [x] Runtime can load + validate registry, failing closed on invalid entries
- [x] Deterministic resolution behavior documented
- [x] CODEOWNERS/review policy documented for registry updates
- [x] Promotion checklist defined (what evidence is required)

Links
- Confluence design: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-auto-selection-v2-design.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0147-kernel-selector-v2-table-driven-registry.json
- PR (schema + initial table): sources/github/redwood/pr_18472_kernel_registry_schema_v1.json

Open questions (tracked in comments)
- Do we want controlled wildcards in v2 of the schema (e.g., gpu_class="sm80+"), or keep explicit rows only?
- Registry revision format: monotonic int vs date-based; date-based chosen for now to reduce merge conflicts.
- Where to store "rationale" links (string field vs structured array). v1 keeps a single string to keep schema simple.
comments: 2026-01-16 (Grace Kim): Creating this ticket to unblock selector v2 implementation. We need a clear contract for the selection table + versioning so we can (a) land initial entries, (b) safely iterate, and (c) allow rollbacks without code changes.

2026-01-20 (Yuki Sato): Drafted schema v1 proposal. Intentionally avoiding wildcards for now. I’ve seen wildcard matching cause accidental cross-regime matches (decode kernels used in prefill) when metadata is incomplete. If we need wildcards later, better to do schema v2 with explicit precedence rules.

2026-01-23 (Marcus Reed): Perf-suite ask: please include generated_at + generated_by so we can correlate benchmark artifacts with the exact registry revision. Also want uniqueness guarantee on (family, flags, bucket, gpu_class) so results aren’t ambiguous.

2026-01-27 (Omar El-Sayed): Loader should fail closed and push selector v2 into fallback. Please make sure we don’t crash the runtime process on a bad registry. Add a counter/trace event for load failures (we can wire into telemetry work in ENG-3927).

2026-02-01 (Hiro Tanaka): CODEOWNERS: require kernels + selection leads for any changes under runtime/config/kernel_registry/. For stable promotions, require perf sign-off. This is a perf-critical knob.

2026-02-06 (Yuki Sato): Opened PR with schema + initial bootstrap table for llama/mistral baseline across L4/A10/A100/H100. Includes validator and unit test that loads a sample registry. PR: pr_18472_kernel_registry_schema_v1.

2026-02-08 (Grace Kim): PR review: please clarify difference between schema_version and registry_revision in docs. Also add deterministic tie-break note (priority then kernel_id) so behavior is stable for perf analysis.
2026-02-10 (Yuki Sato): Updated PR with tie-break documentation + stricter validation (reject unknown seq_bucket). Added a small CLI lint target in CI. Ready for merge after perf-suite green.

2026-02-12 (Connor O'Brien): Release note: schema v1 lands in runtime-1.19; promotion of latest revision should be behind release gate and referenced in rollout checklist (Drive doc). No further blockers.

2026-02-14 (Yuki Sato): PR merged. Follow-up: we should decide how many prior revisions to keep in-repo for rollback (suggest 2). Also should ensure generator script lives in same repo or benchmark-lab; for now documented but not implemented here.
2026-02-21 (Grace Kim): Marking Done. Subsequent registry content additions (Qwen/Mistral tuning) will come as separate PRs against the same schema/revision flow.
